attempted_claim: Let l^{1/2} with quasi-norm ||g||=sum_n |g_n|^{1/2} act by translation on X=R^N with product Polish topology, with turbulent orbit equivalence E_{1/2} defined by x E_{1/2} y iff x-y in l^{1/2} iff sum_n |x_n-y_n|^{1/2}<infinity. Let E1 on (2^N)^N be eventual equality: (a_n) E1 (b_n) iff exists N0 with a_n=b_n for all n>=N0. Decide: is E_{1/2} Borel reducible to E1, i.e. does there exist a Borel map f:R^N->(2^N)^N with x E_{1/2} y iff f(x) E1 f(y)? A complete answer is either such an explicit Borel reduction with proof of the iff property, or a rigorous proof that no Borel reduction exists, e.g. via Hjorth-turbulence generic-ergodicity or Baire-category obstruction.
decisive_failure: originality: The headline E_{1/2} not<=_B E1 is a mere exponent substitution of the canonical textbook turbulent example l^1 translation on R^N. Standard sources record l^1(R) on R^omega as turbulent (Marks notes Ex.1.3, Gao IDST), and Kanovei-Reeken proves NO generically turbulent orbit ER Borel-reduces to any Class-4 ER including E1. Combining them yields the same conclusion for l^1; replacing 1 by 1/2 changes only m^{-1} to m^{-1/2} scaling. No new boundary, encoding, or object distinction; mechanically implied parameter variant, hence not new. value: ADMISSION_DEFECT: the target isolates exponent 1/2 with no pre-stated motivation distinguishing it from l^1 or general l^p (p<1, p>=1) turbulent translations. The negative resolution is therefore an arbitrary parameter fact and textbook restatement: routine verification that one more l^p translation is turbulent plus application of the known Class-1 vs Class-4 irreducibility. No recognized question needs exactly p=1/2 vs E1, no downstream use, no benchmark or classification advance. Not independently worth retrieving later.
